name: Permutation recovery
description: Vasya has written some permutation $$$p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_n$$$ of integers from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$, so for all $$$1 \leq i \leq n$$$ it is true that $$$1 \leq p_i \leq n$$$ and all $$$p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_n$$$ are different. After that he wrote $$$n$$$ numbers $$$next_1, next_2, \ldots, next_n$$$. The number $$$next_i$$$ is equal to the minimal index $$$i \lt j \leq n$$$, such that $$$p_j \gt p_i$$$. If there is no such $$$j$$$ let's let's define as $$$next_i = n + 1$$$. In the evening Vasya went home from school and due to rain, his notebook got wet. Now it is impossible to read some written numbers. Permutation and some values $$$next_i$$$ are completely lost! If for some $$$i$$$ the value $$$next_i$$$ is lost, let's say that $$$next_i = -1$$$. You are given numbers $$$next_1, next_2, \ldots, next_n$$$ (maybe some of them are equal to $$$-1$$$). Help Vasya to find such permutation $$$p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_n$$$ of integers from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$, that he can write it to the notebook and all numbers $$$next_i$$$, which are not equal to $$$-1$$$, will be correct.
input_specification: The first line contains one integer $$$t$$$ — the number of test cases ($$$1 \leq t \leq 100\,000$$$). Next $$$2 \cdot t$$$ lines contains the description of test cases,two lines for each. The first line contains one integer $$$n$$$ — the length of the permutation, written by Vasya ($$$1 \leq n \leq 500\,000$$$). The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$next_1, next_2, \ldots, next_n$$$, separated by spaces ($$$next_i = -1$$$ or $$$i \lt next_i \leq n + 1$$$). It is guaranteed, that the sum of $$$n$$$ in all test cases doesn't exceed $$$500\,000$$$. In hacks you can only use one test case, so $$$T = 1$$$.
output_specification: Print $$$T$$$ lines, in $$$i$$$-th of them answer to the $$$i$$$-th test case. If there is no such permutations $$$p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_n$$$ of integers from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$, that Vasya could write, print the only number $$$-1$$$. In the other case print $$$n$$$ different integers $$$p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_n$$$, separated by spaces ($$$1 \leq p_i \leq n$$$). All defined values of $$$next_i$$$ which are not equal to $$$-1$$$ should be computed correctly $$$p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_n$$$ using defenition given in the statement of the problem. If there exists more than one solution you can find any of them.
approach_summary: Build a Segment Tree over the array. Implement point update and associative range query operations in O(log N) time per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1158C — Permutation recovery [57. Segment Tree (Point Update Range Query)]
topic_editorial.summary: Range queries and updates via Segment Tree.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The query operation is associative (e.g., sum, min, max, gcd). Any contiguous range $[L, R]$ can be decomposed into at most $O(\log N)$ canonical dyadic intervals represented by nodes in a binary tree.
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Tree Construction
We build a binary segment tree over array $A[1..N]$.
Each node covers a segment $[L, R]$. If $L = R$, the node stores $A[L]$. Otherwise:
$$\text{node.val} = \text{combine}(\text{left\_child.val}, \text{right\_child.val})$$

### Step 2: Point / Range Updates
To update position $pos$ with value $val$:
- Traverse down to the leaf node $[pos, pos]$.
- Update leaf value.
- Recompute ancestor values on the way back up in $O(\log N)$ time.

### Step 3: Range Query Processing
To query the associative aggregate on range $[qL, qR]$:
- If current segment $[L, R]$ is completely within $[qL, qR]$, return node value.
- If disjoint, return identity element.
- Otherwise, split and return $\text{combine}(\text{query}(left), \text{query}(right))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}((N + Q) \log N)$
  Building the segment tree takes $\mathcal{O}(N)$. Each point/range query and update traverses at most $4 \log N$ tree nodes, requiring $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ time per query.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  A standard binary segment tree requires at most $4N$ nodes to represent elements up to index $N$.
